I've been reading Neuromancer, and thinking about cyberpunk generally this week. What it used to represent, and how we used to think of the future. The music meant something, because it was dark and menacing, like urban sprawl. You'd play Deus Ex and think, damn, I wish I had some augmentations! You just graft some metal and microcircuitry onto your flesh, inject nanoprobes into your bloodstream or jack your brain into the internet, and suddenly your experience of life is totally different. It was exciting to think about, at the time.

Of course, that's all still impossible here in the Desert of the Real, and even if it were, it would soon become apparent that we already had augmentations— they happened to be separate from our bodies. If you wear contacts, your vision is augmented. Your smartphone can give you the sum of human knowledge... and we use it for Candy Crush?

The fact is, smartphones have been a very quick and easy way to increase our abilities. So quick and so easy, in fact, that we haven't done anything to earn what we've gained. Should it be any surprise, then, that this isn't quite the future we imagined? Our devices spy on us, we don't know how to build them or understand how they work.
